Los Angeles's modern day MTA from my Pasadena-D timeline. Different colors for the different lines, of course, with the translucent gray lines in the background being proposed future MTA lines.

Given the history of Pasadena-D, a lot of the lines follow old P.E. routes, while others use former rail routes of other carriers. Leaving Union Station, the lines all travel in (Pas-D) freeway corridors for at least a few miles...all the way to El Monte, for the San Bernadino line. That makes the westward running section very crowded and the MTA is currently asking for submissions to correct this bottleneck. Interestingly - and all due to a Great Depression program - only the line actually through Pasadena is a subway, all else is surface/elevated.
